‘NO DOCUMENTS RELATED TO FLOOD CONTROL WERE IN THE BRS BUILDING’

The Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH) assured the public that no documents related to the ongoing investigation into the flood control anomalies were in the Bureau of Research and Standards (BRS) building that caught fire in Quezon City on Wednesday.

“Initial findings indicate that the fire originated from a computer unit inside the Materials Testing Division that reportedly exploded,” they wrote in a statement.

They also reported that no employees were hurt in the incident, and an investigation team is currently assessing the full extent of the damage.

🔹BrahMos NG: 50% lighter, smaller, more stealthy, same Mach 3.5 speed.
🔹BrahMos-II: Hypersonic variant planned with Mach 7–8 speeds.

9.Indigenization & Production:
🔹Initially 65% components supplied by Russia; India increased indigenous content to 85%.
🔹New Lucknow facility producing 100–150 missiles annually.
🔹Supported by over 200 Indian companies.

10.Export & Global Recognition:
🔹Philippines: First export customer (375 million USD order).
🔹Interest from Vietnam, Malaysia, Indonesia, Middle East & South America.

💡 Summary:
From a collaborative Russian engine project to India’s most feared supersonic missile, BrahMos combines speed, precision, stealth, and universal deployment. It has redefined India’s defense capabilities and proven itself in real combat scenarios, establishing India as a global leader in advanced missile technology. #OperationSindoor
